about: Coreintegra is a Mumbai-based HR solutions provider offering staffing, vendor management, payroll, labour-law compliance and in-house HR-tech/reg-tech platforms (Ctrl-F, CoreX, Core Pay, Core PFT). It served 385 customers in FY26 across 30+ industries via 7 branch offices, with about 88% of revenue from Maharashtra. The model is asset-light with very thin margins (PAT margin under 1%).
sector: HR services, staffing and compliance technology

objects.purpose: Capital expenditure towards upgrading existing IT infrastructure

promoters.background: Promoters hold 49,46,874 shares (64.51%); with promoter group (incl. Eureka Outsourcing Solutions) total 93.04% pre-issue. MD Mahesh Krishnamoorthy has about two decades of finance experience.

concentration.note: Top 5 customers were 89.31% of FY26 revenue (88.04% FY25, 90.16% FY24); Customer 1 alone was 53.01% and Customer 2 33.57% in FY26. Maharashtra gives 87.97% of revenue.

litigation_note: RHP notes outstanding legal proceedings involving the company, group company, promoters, directors and KMP; amounts not quantified in the provided index. Contingent liability of Rs 22.61 lakh (performance guarantee for a related enterprise).
strengths: In-house technology platforms (Ctrl-F, CoreX, Core Pay, Core PFT) across the HR and compliance value chain.
Revenue grew from Rs 366 crore in FY24 to Rs 515 crore in FY26, about 18.6% CAGR.
Debt-free: no borrowings in any of the last three years.
High client retention of 90.46% in FY26 and top 10 customers associated for over 3 years.
Presence across 23 states and 4 union territories, serving 1,500+ client locations.
Reported ROCE of 20.19% and ROE of 17.94% in FY26.
ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 9001:2015 certified with 4 registered software copyrights.
Asset-light model with low capital expenditure needs.

risks.title: Extreme customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 5 customers gave 89.31% of FY26 revenue; Customer 1 alone 53.01% and Customer 2 33.57%. Losing one would badly hit revenue.

risks.title: Razor-thin margins
risks.detail: EBITDA margin only 1.17% and PAT margin 0.87% in FY26, so small cost increases can erase profit.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow and heavy receivables
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 3.05 crore in FY26 (taxes paid Rs 8.09 crore). Receivables are 40.02% of total assets.

risks.title: Revenue concentrated in one state and sector
risks.detail: Maharashtra gave 87.97% of FY26 revenue; IT/ITES and Infra clients make up about 90.9%.

risks.title: Short client contracts without volume guarantee
risks.detail: Contracts are typically 1 year (max 3) and can be terminated on notice, so revenue visibility is limited.

risks.title: Outstanding litigation and past compliance lapses
risks.detail: Legal proceedings pending against company, promoters and directors; past delays in EPF, labour welfare and professional tax payments and RoC filings.

risks.title: Related party dealings
risks.detail: Transactions with director-linked firms including inter-corporate deposits and a Rs 22.61 lakh performance guarantee for a related enterprise.

risks.title: Issue proceeds unappraised and valuation not yet set
risks.detail: Only Rs 18.01 crore of identified uses with no independent appraisal; price band blank and promoters keep control with 64.51% pre-issue.

notes: FY26 (Mar-26) restated consolidated figures; INR lakh converted to crore. Balance sheet text was garbled; totals cross-checked (current assets = total less non-current). EBITDA, margins, ROCE, ROE as reported (PAT margin on total income). RoNW computed by RHP as PAT/net worth (RHP table mislabels years). Cash and bank = cash plus bank balances plus other bank deposits (Annexure N). Reserves FY26 falls after Rs 7.65 crore bonus capitalisation. Reservation percentages derived from share counts over net issue of 26,76,800 shares (market maker 1,42,400 separate; no anchor). Total issue size, price band, P/E and GCP amount blank in RHP. Peer revenue converted from lakh.
